info.title: Oh Ho Bastra API
info.description:
REST API of the Oh Ho Bastra storefront (Express + TypeScript).

- Auth uses HTTP-only cookies; browsers must send credentials.
- Request and response bodies are snake_case JSON.
- Money is always an integer amount in cents.
- Every response has `success` and `message`. Failures add a machine-readable `code`, and validation failures list `errors` with a react-hook-form style `field` path.
- Every response carries an `X-Request-ID` header (a valid incoming one is reused).

post.description: Creates a customer account and starts a session. Sets the `access_token` and `refresh_token` (HTTP-only) cookies and the readable `is_logged_in` cookie. The email is trimmed and lowercased. From a guest session (by its refresh cookie), the guest's bag joins the account's (quantities add up, capped to stock; the account keeps its own discount code, else takes the guest's), the guest's orders placed with the account's email move to the account, and the guest is signed out and deleted once it has no orders left, all in one transaction.

409.description: Email already registered (USER_ALREADY_EXISTS)

429.description: Too many sign-ups from this address (TOO_MANY_REQUESTS); see Retry-After

post.description: For shopping without an account: creates a hidden guest user (role `guest`, no email or password, name "Guest") and starts its session. Sets the `access_token` and `refresh_token` (HTTP-only) cookies and the readable `is_logged_in` cookie. A guest can use the bag, its discount code, checkout (giving an email) and its own orders; the wishlist, reviews, the address book and account settings answer 403 GUEST_NOT_ALLOWED. A request that already has a session (guest or not) gets its user back unchanged, with 200.

201.description: Guest session started (200: already signed in)

429.description: Too many guest sessions from this address (TOO_MANY_REQUESTS); see Retry-After

post.description: Starts a new session. Sets the `access_token` and `refresh_token` (HTTP-only) cookies and the readable `is_logged_in` cookie. From a guest session (by its refresh cookie), the guest's bag joins the account's (quantities add up, capped to stock; the account keeps its own discount code, else takes the guest's), the guest's orders placed with the account's email move to the account, and the guest is signed out and deleted once it has no orders left, all in one transaction. A guest has no email or password, so it can never log in itself.

401.description: Unknown email or wrong password (INVALID_CREDENTIALS)

429.description: Too many failed attempts for this account or address (TOO_MANY_REQUESTS); see Retry-After

get.description: For the browser to navigate to, not to fetch: redirects to Google's account picker (OpenID Connect with PKCE), keeping its state in a 10-minute `google_oauth` cookie. When Google sign-in isn't configured, redirects to the login page with `?google_error=unavailable`.

schema.description: A storefront path to return to after signing in; anything else is ignored

get.description: Where Google sends the browser back. Checks the state against the `google_oauth` cookie, trades the code for the Google profile and signs in the customer linked to that Google account, creating one for a new email. Sets the `access_token` and `refresh_token` (HTTP-only) cookies and the readable `is_logged_in` cookie. From a guest session (by its refresh cookie), the guest's bag joins the account's (quantities add up, capped to stock; the account keeps its own discount code, else takes the guest's), the guest's orders placed with the account's email move to the account, and the guest is signed out and deleted once it has no orders left, all in one transaction. Then redirects to `?next=` from the start (else the home page, or /admin for an admin). Any failure redirects to the login page with `?google_error=` set to `cancelled`, `failed`, `unverified` (the Google email isn't verified) or `exists` (a password account already uses the email).

post.description: Revokes the session of the refresh token cookie, if any, and always clears the auth cookies.

Rotates the refresh token and issues a new access token. A request that lost a concurrent rotation within 30 seconds gets a new access token only. Reusing an older refresh token revokes the session. Every 401 clears the auth cookies.

post.description: Refunds chosen lines (quantities up to what is left of each), the shipping (once) and/or a goodwill amount of a paid, shipped, delivered or partly refunded order; without any of them, everything left. Lines are worth what was paid for them (the order's discount shared out over the lines, rounded to the cent so the parts add up). The money goes back by card (a Stripe refund) and store credit in the shares the order was paid. Each refund is keyed by request_id, so a retry refunds once. The order becomes partially_refunded, then refunded once nothing is left.
